'''Rudolf Grimm''' (born 10 November 1961) is an [[experimental physicist]] from Austria. His work centres on ultracold [[atom]]s and [[quantum gas]]es. He was the first scientist worldwide who, with his team, succeeded in realizing a [[Bose–Einstein condensation]] of non-polar [[molecule]]s.

==Career==
Grimm graduated in [[physics]] from the [[University of Hannover]] in 1986. From 1986 to 1989 he was a post-graduate researcher at the [[ETH Zurich]] (Swiss Federal Institute of Technology), then went on to the [[Institute of Spectroscopy]] of the [[USSR Academy of Sciences]] in [[Troitsk]] near Moscow for half a year. He spent the next ten years in [[Heidelberg]] as a researcher at the [[Max Planck Institute for Nuclear Physics]]. In 1994, Grimm applied to the [[University of Heidelberg]] to qualify as a professor by receiving the "[[venia docendi]]" in [[experimental physics]]. In the year 2000, he was appointed to a chair in experimental physics at the [[University of Innsbruck]], where he has been [[Dean (education)|Dean]] of the Faculty for Mathematics, Computer Science and Physics since 2005 and Director of the Research Center for Quantum Physics from 2006. Since 2003, Grimm has also held the position of Scientific Director at the [[Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information]] (IQOQI) of the [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]] (ÖAW). Grimm is married, with three children.

==Research==
The work of the experimental physicist concentrates on [[Bose–Einstein condensation]] of [[atom]]s and [[molecule]]s and on [[Fermi gas|fermionic quantum gas]]es. In 2002 his working group succeeded for the first time ever to produce a Bose–Einstein condensate from [[caesium]] atoms.<ref name="Weber Herbig Mark Nägerl pp. 232–235">{{cite journal | last1=Weber | first1=Tino | last2=Herbig | first2=Jens | last3=Mark | first3=Michael | last4=Nägerl | first4=Hanns-Christoph | last5=Grimm | first5=Rudolf | title=Bose-Einstein Condensation of Cesium | journal=Science | publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) | volume=299 | issue=5604 | date=10 January 2003 | issn=0036-8075 | doi=10.1126/science.1079699 | pages=232–235| pmid=12471267 | s2cid=43395759 | doi-access=free }}</ref> In the following year, the team produced the first Bose–Einstein condensate of molecules (simultaneously with [[Deborah S. Jin]]'s group at [[JILA]], [[Boulder, Colorado]]).<ref name="Jochim Bartenstein Altmeyer Hendl pp. 2101–2103">{{cite journal | last1=Jochim | first1=S. | last2=Bartenstein | first2=M. | last3=Altmeyer | first3=A. | last4=Hendl | first4=G. | last5=Riedl | first5=S. | last6=Chin | first6=C. | last7=Hecker Denschlag | first7=J. | last8=Grimm | first8=R. | title=Bose-Einstein Condensation of Molecules | journal=Science | publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) | volume=302 | issue=5653 | date=19 December 2003 | issn=0036-8075 | doi=10.1126/science.1093280 | pages=2101–2103| pmid=14615548 | bibcode=2003Sci...302.2101J | s2cid=13041446 | doi-access=free }}</ref> In 2004, the Innsbruck scientists achieved a [[Fermionic condensate]]. In his work on collective oscillations and pairing energies, Grimm found first evidence of the flow of particles without any loss of energy ([[superfluidity]]) in Fermi condensates. Meanwhile, Grimm and his team have succeeded in producing more complex molecules in ultracold quantum gases. Currently Grimm is concentrating his efforts on producing mixed condensation from atoms of different elements. In 2006, his working group also managed to lift the veil on an old mystery of physics: they succeeded in the first experimental observation of [[Efimov state]]s, mysterious [[quantum state]]s that the Russian scientist [[Vitaly Efimov|Vitali Efimov]] had theoretically predicted in the early 1970s.<ref name="Kraemer Mark Waldburger Danzl 2006 pp. 315–318">{{cite journal | last1=Kraemer | first1=T. | last2=Mark | first2=M. | last3=Waldburger | first3=P. | last4=Danzl | first4=J. G. | last5=Chin | first5=C. | last6=Engeser | first6=B. | last7=Lange | first7=A. D. | last8=Pilch | first8=K. | last9=Jaakkola | first9=A. | last10=Nägerl | first10=H.-C. | last11=Grimm | first11=R. | title=Evidence for Efimov quantum states in an ultracold gas of caesium atoms | journal=Nature | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=440 | issue=7082 | year=2006 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/nature04626 | pages=315–318| pmid=16541068 | arxiv=cond-mat/0512394 | bibcode=2006Natur.440..315K | s2cid=4379828 }}</ref>

==Awards==
Grimm has received numerous awards for his achievements. In 2005 he was presented with the [[Wittgenstein Award]], Austria's highest scientific accolade. In the same year, the Austrian daily paper [[Die Presse]] made him „Austrian (Researcher) of the Year 2005". Years before, he had won the Gerhard Hess Prize, a new blood stipend of the [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft|German Research Foundation]] (DFG) (1996), and the Silver Medal of the [[ETH Zurich]] (1989). Recently he received the Beller Lectureship Award of the [[American Physical Society]] (APS) (2007), the Science Award of the Region of [[Tyrol (state)|Tyrol]] (2008) and was named „Austrian Scientist of the Year 2009" by the Austrian Club of Education and Science Journalists. In 2018, he was honored jointly with [[Vitaly Efimov]] with the inaugural Faddeev Medal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uibk.ac.at/newsroom/rudolf-grimm-receives-inaugural-faddeev-medal.html.en|title=Rudolf Grimm Receives Inaugural Faddeev Medal – University of Innsbruck|website=www.uibk.ac.at|date=6 February 2024 }}</ref> In 2021, he received an [[ERC Advanced Grant]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://iqoqi.at/en/current/news/783-rudolf-grimm-receives-erc-advanced-grant|title=Rudolf Grimm receives ERC Advanced Grant – IQOQI Innsbruck|website=iqoqi.at|date=22 April 2021 }}</ref>

In 2006, Grimm became a full member of the [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="i446">{{cite web | title=Rudolf Grimm | website=Österreichische Akademie der Wissenschaften | url=https://www.oeaw.ac.at/m/grimm-rudolf | language=de | access-date=29 August 2026}}</ref>
